Subject: Re: Fwd: Novum — urgent: p99 + 429 spike (ND-4319)

Soojin/Dylan — quick triage update from infra: 
- Root cause (interim): aggressive client retries without jitter created a retry storm that amplified 429s. Clients observed 429 -> retried immediately -> pushed more traffic into the same hot kernel queues -> queueing increased and p99 jumped.
- Observed behavior: tokenization kernels and KV cache hot-shard experienced queueing; scheduler backed up and slow-started extra workers but that added latency to in-flight requests (p95→p99 blowout).

Mitigations we can/are doing now (minutes):
1) Soft per-key burst increase for ND-4319 for 30 minutes to let in-flight requests drain. This is live.
2) Deploy server-side Retry-After header and increase the minimum retry-backoff recommendation in the API (10s->30s) — pushes for a client update but we can set Retry-After on 429s immediately.
3) Enable per-key circuit breaker: if sustained 429 > 2% for 2m, return quick 503s for new requests instead of queuing. This reduces latency for healthy tenants.

Longer term (hours-days):
- Improve quota + token bucket behavior to favor evenly distributed token consumption and add jitter hints to SDKs.
- Add a small probabilistic shedding mode for hot KV shards to avoid head-of-line blocking.

Estimate: config changes (1)+(3) rolled in 20–30m; SDK and quota redesign needs a sprint. I’ll coordinate a patch and a rollback plan.

—
Rishi Malhotra

Subject: Mitigation applied — please verify Novum critical paths

Hi Priya,

Quick update on actions we’ve applied (live now):
- Temporary per-key burst cap for ND-4319 increased by 4x for 30 minutes to flush inflight traffic.
- Per-key circuit breaker enabled: new heavy request patterns will be short-circuited to 503 to prevent queueing for other tenants.
- 429 responses now include Retry-After with a conservative minimum backoff (30s).

Can you validate your critical workflows? We are monitoring p95/p99 and 429 rate closely (dashboard link below). Initial metrics show 429 rate dropping from 4.6% → 1.1% over 20 minutes and p99 improving to ~1.1s (down from 1.9s), but some spikes remain when one of your batch workers retries strongly.

If we see continued retry storms, we can: (a) temporarily route ND-4319 to a dedicated pool, or (b) issue temporary credits if the impact meets SLAs. Marissa is copied to coordinate commercial next steps.
